mainTopic: The צפון requirement: why it is essential for every חטאת, what the word 'אותו' teaches, and how we know it is essential for an עולה
overview: This עמוד is about where offerings must be slaughtered in the צפון of the עזרה, and how strict that rule is. A ברייתא first shows that the extra verse about the שעיר נשיא makes the צפון essential for every חטאת. The גמרא adds that for other חטאות this comes from the rule being repeated for the כשבה and the שעירה. That leaves the word 'אותו' in the שעיר נשיא verse looking extra, so the גמרא tries several jobs for it. It suggests excluding נחשון's goat, the שוחט, a bird offering, and a קרבן פסח, and each one is knocked down in turn. In the end it returns to the reading about the שוחט and refines it: the animal must be in the צפון, and the person slaughtering need not be, but the מקבל who collects the blood must be. Next the גמרא asks how we know the צפון is essential for an עולה. רב אדא בר אהבה offers a קל וחומר from the חטאת. That proof is challenged, רבינא defends it with the rule that a טפל cannot be stricter than its עיקר, and מר זוטרא questions that rule. The discussion continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Why do we need this verse if we already know it?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא challenges its own source: a general פסוק already teaches that every חטאת is slaughtered where the עולה is, so why repeat it for the שעיר נשיא?
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you really learn it from here? But it was already said: 'In the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, the sin offering shall be slaughtered!' So why was this one singled out?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא had just learned from the שעיר נשיא verse that this חטאת is slaughtered in the צפון. Now it objects: we already knew that from a general פסוק about all חטאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ויקרא 6:18 already says every חטאת is slaughtered in the place of the עולה, which is the צפון. So the verse about the שעיר נשיא seems to add nothing. The question 'הא למה יצא' asks what new lesson this repeated verse must be teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you really learn it from here? It challenges a source by pointing out the law is already known elsewhere.
But wasn't it already stated? It brings an earlier פסוק.
Burnt offering. It is slaughtered in the north of the courtyard.
Sin offering.
So why was this singled out? It asks what extra lesson a repeated verse teaches.

phrases.english: And do you learn it from here?!
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the verse about the king's goat, which says to slaughter it where the עולה is slaughtered (ויקרא 4:24).

phrases.english: But hasn't it already been stated:
"In the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered
shall the sin offering be slaughtered"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:18

phrases.english: If so, why was this one singled out?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מִכָּאן אַתָּה לָמֵד?! וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the שעיר נשיא verse as the source that it needs צפון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A general פסוק (ויקרא 6:18) already requires צפון for every חטאת, so the specific verse looks extra.

steps.title: The extra verse makes the north essential
steps.stepSummary: The repeated verse 'fixes the place': a חטאת not slaughtered in the צפון is פסול, even after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: To fix a place for it, so that if he did not slaughter it in the north, it is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The extra verse teaches that the צפון is required, not just preferred.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general פסוק alone would only tell us the right way to do it. Because the Torah repeats it, we learn the location is 'fixed': if he slaughtered it anywhere else, the offering is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: To fix a place for it, making that location a firm requirement.
The north side of the Temple courtyard.
Disqualified. The offering is invalid.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key idea of the rest of the section: a repeated verse can turn a preferred practice into an essential one.

phrases.english: To fix a place for it,
so that if he did not slaughter it in the north, it is disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns a new purpose to the seemingly extra verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שעיר נשיא verse seemed to add nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that צפון is essential: without it, the offering is פסול.

steps.title: Maybe only this offering needs the north
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests another reading: perhaps the verse means only this offering requires צפון, and no other does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it was singled out for this? Or maybe it only means that this one requires the north, and no other one requires the north?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions the answer it just gave. It suggests the special verse might limit the צפון rule to the שעיר נשיא alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the Torah singles out one case, you could read it as 'only this one'. If so, the verse would not teach that צפון is essential. It would teach that the rule belongs to this offering alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you say it came for this? It opens a different possible reading.
Or is it perhaps only... It offers the alternative.
Requires.

phrases.english: Do you say it was singled out for this purpose?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא שֶׁזֶּה טָעוּן צָפוֹן,
phrases.english: Or perhaps it only means that this one requires the north,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the king's goat.

phrases.english: and no other one requires the north?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר לְכָךְ יָצָא; אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of step 2, that the verse makes צפון essential
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A verse that singles out one case could be limiting the rule to that case rather than making it stricter.

steps.title: Another verse proves all sin offerings need the north
steps.stepSummary: A verse about the individual's חטאת also says to slaughter it where the עולה is. This shows the צפון rule is a בנה אב for every חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And he shall slaughter the sin offering in the place of the burnt offering.' This set a model for all sin offerings, that they require the north.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the 'only this one' reading by bringing a verse that says the same thing about another חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a different חטאת also has the צפון rule written for it, the rule is clearly not limited to the שעיר נשיא. It becomes a בנה אב, a model that applies to all חטאות. So the first answer stands: the special verse makes צפון essential.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse says. It brings a פסוק as proof.
Built a model. One case sets the rule for a whole group.

steps.whatToRemember: Every חטאת must be slaughtered in the צפון, and the extra verse for the שעיר נשיא teaches that this is essential, not only preferred.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"And he shall slaughter the sin offering in the place of the burnt offering" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:29

phrases.english: this set a model for all sin offerings,
that they require the north.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the limiting reading proposed in step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a verse about another חטאת to show the rule is general
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the שעיר נשיא needs צפון.
steps.terutzMaskana: All חטאות need צפון. The rule is a בנה אב.

steps.title: How do we know the north is essential for other sin offerings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sums up. For the שעיר נשיא, צפון is both the ideal and essential. For other חטאות, we have only shown it is the ideal. Where do we learn it is essential?
steps.simpleTranslation: We have found that for the king's goat, the north is both the proper way and essential. For other sin offerings too, we have found it is the proper way. From where do we know it is essential?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now speaks in its own voice. It points out a gap: we have not yet shown that other חטאות are פסול if not slaughtered in the צפון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra verse that made צפון essential was written only about the שעיר נשיא. The general verses teach other חטאות only the proper way (למצוה). So we still need a source that, for them, missing the צפון disqualifies the offering (לעכב).

keyTerms.meaning: We have found. It reviews what is already proven.
The goat חטאת brought by a king (ויקרא 4:22-26).
As the proper way to do it, but not required after the fact.
As essential. If it is not done, the offering is invalid.
From where do we know it?

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up למצוה and לעכב. Something can be the correct way to do a מצוה‎ (למצוה) without disqualifying the offering when it is skipped (לעכב).

phrases.english: We have found for the king's goat –
both as the proper way and as essential;
for other sin offerings too –
we have found it as the proper way;
as essential, from where do we know it?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that other חטאות are פסול if not slaughtered in the צפון

steps.title: The Torah repeats it for the lamb and the she-goat
steps.stepSummary: The צפון rule is written twice, once for the lamb חטאת and once for the she-goat חטאת. The repetition shows it is essential for other חטאות as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is written about the female lamb, and it is written about the female goat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the Torah writes the צפון rule for both the כשבה and the שעירה. That repetition teaches it is essential.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing the rule once would be enough to teach the proper way. Writing it a second time works just like the extra verse for the שעיר נשיא: it makes צפון essential, so other חטאות are also פסול if slaughtered elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written.
Female lamb. One option for an individual's חטאת (ויקרא 4:32-35).
Female goat. The other option for an individual's חטאת (ויקרא 4:27-31).

steps.whatToRemember: For all חטאות, slaughter in the צפון is essential (לעכב). For the שעיר נשיא it comes from its extra verse, and for other חטאות from the double mention for the כשבה and the שעירה.

phrases.english: Because it is written about the female lamb
and it is written about the female goat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The צפון rule is repeated for the כשבה and the שעירה, and the repetition makes it essential for other חטאות.

steps.title: What is the word 'it' for?
steps.stepSummary: We have already shown that צפון is essential for all חטאות. So why does the Torah need the word 'אותו' in the שעיר נשיא verse?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, why do I need the word 'it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word 'אותו' is teaching. The rule it seemed to teach has now been learned from somewhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 proved that צפון is essential for every חטאת, using the repetition between the lamb חטאת and the she-goat חטאת. That makes the word 'אותו' in the שעיר נשיא verse look extra. The גמרא assumes no word in the Torah is wasted, so it needs a new job for 'אותו'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It': the word in the שעיר נשיא verse, 'and slaughter it in the place of the עולה'
'Why do I need it?': asking what an apparently extra word teaches

phrases.english: But why do I need the word "it"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:24, about the goat brought by the נשיא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since step 6 learned the essential צפון rule from the repetition, the word 'אותו' needs a new purpose.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word 'אותו' teaches, now that it is not needed to make צפון essential.

steps.title: 'It' excludes the goat of נחשון
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that 'אותו' means only this goat needs צפון. The goat of נחשון does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for what was taught in a ברייתא: 'It' must be slaughtered in the north, but the goat of נחשון is not slaughtered in the north.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'אותו' limits the צפון rule. The goat brought by נחשון is left out of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אותו' means 'it', this goat, and not a similar goat. The similar goat is the שעיר that נחשון and the other נשיאים brought at the inauguration of the משכן. So the word now has a clear job: it excludes that goat from the צפון requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is needed for': the word is used for another teaching
'As was taught in a ברייתא'
The goat brought by נחשון, the נשיא of יהודה, at the inauguration of the משכן
The northern side of the courtyard, where certain offerings are slaughtered

phrases.english: It is needed for that which was taught in a ברייתא:
"It" is slaughtered in the north,
but the goat of נחשון is not slaughtered in the north.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 by giving 'אותו' a limiting job.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אותו' teaches that the goat of נחשון did not need to be slaughtered in the צפון.

steps.title: נחשון's goat was included in סמיכה
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא learns from 'the goat' that נחשון's goat needed סמיכה, according to רבי יהודה. According to רבי שמעון, the same words include the goats brought for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught: 'And he shall lay his hand on the head of the goat.' This includes the goat of נחשון in the rule of laying hands. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי שמעון says: it includes the goats brought for idol worship in the rule of laying hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא to set up the next move. This ברייתא explains why we would have needed a special word to leave נחשון's goat out of the צפון rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra words 'the goat' in the same verse add a goat to the rule of סמיכה. For רבי יהודה, that is נחשון's goat. For רבי שמעון, it is the goats brought for עבודה זרה. In רבי יהודה's view, then, נחשון's goat already shares one rule with the שעיר נשיא.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaning one's hands on the head of the animal before it is slaughtered
'To include': the verse adds another case to the rule
Goats brought as חטאות by the community for idol worship done by mistake

phrases.english: And it was taught: "And he shall lay his hand upon the head of the goat":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:24. It could have just said 'its head', so 'the goat' is treated as extra.

phrases.english: this is to include the goat of נחשון in the rule of laying hands.
These are the words of רבי יהודה.
רבי שמעון says:
it is to include the goats brought for idol worship in the rule of laying hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies background showing why the exclusion in step 8 was needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, נחשון's goat required סמיכה. According to רבי שמעון, the goats for עבודה זרה required סמיכה.

steps.title: Included in סמיכה, but not in צפון
steps.stepSummary: Because נחשון's goat needed סמיכה, we might have thought it also needed צפון. 'אותו' teaches that it did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since these goats were included in laying hands, they are also included in slaughter in the north. So the word 'it' teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. 'אותו' is needed so we do not carry the צפון rule over to נחשון's goat just because it shares the rule of סמיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without 'אותו', we might reason that sharing one rule means sharing the other. 'אותו' blocks that reasoning. נחשון's goat gets סמיכה but not צפון.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It might enter your mind to say': the mistaken idea we might have had
'Since'
'They were included'
'It teaches us': the verse tells us otherwise

steps.whatToRemember: The צפון rule is essential for every חטאת. The word 'אותו' leaves out נחשון's goat, which needed סמיכה but did not need צפון.

phrases.english: It might have entered your mind to say:
since they were included in laying hands,
they are also included in slaughter in the north;
so the word "it" teaches us that they are not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the סמיכה ברייתא from step 9 to explain why the exclusion from step 8 is needed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'אותו' is needed so we do not assume that נחשון's goat needed צפון just because it needed סמיכה.

steps.title: רבינא: The explanation only works for רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges the explanation of 'אותו'. It makes sense for רבי יהודה, but what would רבי שמעון say?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא objected: This fits רבי יהודה. But according to רבי שמעון, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks the explanation from the last step. He says it only fits one side of the argument between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, נחשון's goat needed סמיכה. So we might have thought it also needed צפון, and 'אותו' was needed to teach that it did not. For רבי שמעון, the extra words include the goats brought for עבודה זרה, not נחשון's goat. So the סמיכה link that made us think of צפון does not exist for נחשון's goat. Then why would the Torah need 'אותו'?

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it, a strong challenge
This works out well
What is there to say?

phrases.english: Ravina objects to it:
This works out well according to Rabbi Yehuda;
phrases.notes: For רבי יהודה, נחשון's goat needed סמיכה (step 9), so 'אותו' was needed to block צפון.

phrases.english: according to Rabbi Shimon, what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 10 by pointing to רבי שמעון's view from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'אותו' excludes נחשון's goat from צפון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי שמעון, nothing suggests נחשון's goat followed any חטאת rules. So there is nothing for 'אותו' to exclude, and the word has no job.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: It does not even work for רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא בריה דרב טבי tells רבינא that the explanation fails even for רבי יהודה. The verse added only סמיכה, so there is no reason to think צפון was added too.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא son of רב טבי said to רבינא: And does it work well for רבי יהודה? What was included is included, and what was not included is not included!
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא goes further than רבינא. He says the explanation of 'אותו' has a problem even according to רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the verse included נחשון's goat only for סמיכה. That inclusion gives no reason to add other rules like צפון. So even for רבי יהודה, the Torah would not need 'אותו' to exclude צפון.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it work out well? (said as a challenge)
It was included (by an extra word in the פסוק)
It was not included

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב טָבִי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra, son of Rav Tavi, said to Ravina:
And according to Rabbi Yehuda, does it work out well?!
For what it was included, it was included,
phrases.notes: He means סמיכה, the one thing the פסוק added for נחשון's goat.

phrases.english: and what it was not included for, it was not included for!
phrases.notes: He means צפון. Nothing in the פסוק added it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens רבינא's challenge so that it covers רבי יהודה too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 10 that, because of סמיכה, we would have thought נחשון's goat needed צפון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Including one rule (סמיכה) does not bring in other rules (צפון). So there was never a reason to think צפון applied, and nothing needed excluding.

steps.title: Blocking the answer from a בנין אב
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say that, without 'אותו', we would learn צפון for נחשון's goat from all other חטאות through a בנין אב. מר זוטרא rejects this: by that logic, סמיכה would also come from a בנין אב. The real reason is that a one-time offering is not learned from offerings for all generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: if the פסוק had not excluded it, I would have said we learn צפון through a בנין אב. If so, סמיכה itself should also be learned through a בנין אב! Rather, we do not learn from offerings for all generations. Here too, we do not learn from offerings for all generations!
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא raises a possible defense of the explanation of 'אותו' and then knocks it down. This finishes his challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The defense says we would have learned צפון for נחשון's goat from regular חטאות. But if that worked, we would also learn סמיכה that way, and the Torah would not need a special פסוק for סמיכה. Since it does need one, we see that נחשון's one-time offering is not learned from offerings for all generations (דורות). That same rule blocks צפון too, so 'אותו' is still not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (bringing up a possible answer)
The פסוק excluded it
Learning a general rule from a model case
Leaning one's hands on the animal before it is slaughtered
We do not learn from the rules for all generations

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's own answer. It is a possible answer that מר זוטרא brings up only to reject it. The rejection strengthens his challenge.

phrases.english: And if you would say:
if the verse had not excluded it,
I would have said: let it be derived through a paradigm;
phrases.notes: The idea is that צפון would be learned from all the regular חטאות.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, סְמִיכָה גּוּפַהּ תֵּיתֵי מִבִּנְיַן אָב!
phrases.english: if so, let placing hands itself be derived from a paradigm!
Rather, we do not learn from offerings for all generations;
phrases.notes: נחשון's goat was a one-time offering for the dedication of the משכן.

phrases.english: here too, we do not learn from offerings for all generations!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא אִי לָא מַעֲטֵיהּ קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shuts down a possible defense against מר זוטרא's challenge in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that a בנין אב would have required צפון for נחשון's goat.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If a בנין אב worked here, סמיכה would not need its own פסוק. That it does need one proves we do not learn the one-time offering from offerings for all generations.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the rule that one-time offerings of the משכן's dedication are not learned from regular offerings. This leaves 'אותו' needing a completely new explanation.

steps.title: New reading: the animal must be in the north, not the slaughterer
steps.stepSummary: Since the word 'אותו' cannot be about נחשון's goat, the גמרא reads it differently: the animal must be in the צפון, but the person slaughtering it does not have to stand in the צפון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, 'it in the north': it must be in the north, but the one who slaughters does not need to be in the north.
steps.whatsHappening: After the old explanation falls apart, the גמרא gives 'אותו' a new job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אותו' now points to the animal itself. Only the animal has to be in the צפון when it is slaughtered. The שוחט may stand outside the northern area.

keyTerms.meaning: It (the animal itself)
The one who slaughters
Rather (switching to a new explanation)

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'אותו' teaches that the animal must be in the צפון. The person slaughtering it does not need to stand in the צפון.

phrases.english: Rather, 'it in the north':
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:24

phrases.english: but the one who slaughters is not required to be in the north.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that was knocked down in steps 11 to 13 with a new reading of 'אותו'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reading of the extra word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אותו' excludes נחשון's goat from needing צפון.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אותו' limits the צפון rule to the animal. The שוחט does not need to stand in the צפון.

steps.title: The slaughterer rule is already known from רבי אחיא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the rule about where the שוחט stands is already learned elsewhere, from רבי אחיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule that the slaughterer does not need to stand in the north is already learned from רבי אחיא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation from the previous step. It says we do not need 'אותו' here to teach about the שוחט, because another source already teaches it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 the word 'אותו' in the פסוק of the נשיא's goat was used to teach that the שוחט need not stand in the צפון. The problem is that רבי אחיא already learns this exact rule from a different 'אותו', in the פסוק about the עולה. A word in the תורה should not be spent teaching something we already know.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who slaughters the offering
It is derived (literally, 'it comes out')
A תנא whose ברייתא is about to be quoted

phrases.english: The one who slaughters —
phrases.notes: He means the rule from step 14, that the slaughterer does not have to stand in the north.

phrases.english: that is derived from Rabbi Achiya!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation of 'אותו' given in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'אותו' in the נשיא's goat teaches that the שוחט need not stand in the צפון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That rule is already taught by רבי אחיא from the עולה, so this 'אותו' would be teaching nothing new.

steps.title: רבי אחיא's ברייתא about where the slaughterer stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אחיא, who learns from 'אותו' in the עולה פסוק that only the animal must be in the צפון, not the שוחט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחיא says: 'And he shall slaughter it on the side of the altar, northward.' Why does the פסוק say 'it'? We found that the כהן who collects the blood must stand in the north while collecting in the north. If he stood in the south and collected in the north, the offering is פסול. You might think slaughtering works the same way. So the פסוק says 'it': the animal must be in the north, but the slaughterer does not need to be.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that proves its objection. It shows that רבי אחיא already learns the שוחט rule from the עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For קבלה, both the כהן and the blood must be in the צפון. Without a special word, we would think שחיטה follows the same rule. רבי אחיא reads 'אותו' as saying only 'it', the animal, must be in the צפון. So the rule is already covered, and the 'אותו' of the נשיא's goat must be teaching something else.

keyTerms.meaning: The side of the altar
The north side of the עזרה, where קדשי קדשים are slaughtered
The one who collects the blood in a vessel
South
The פסוק comes to teach

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Achiya says:
"And he shall slaughter it on the side of the altar northward" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:11

phrases.english: what does the verse come to teach?
Since we have found that he stands in the north
and collects the blood in the north,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם עָמַד בַּדָּרוֹם וְקִיבֵּל בַּצָּפוֹן פָּסוּל;
phrases.english: and if he stood in the south and collected in the north, it is disqualified;
one might think this one is the same?
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the slaughterer.

phrases.english: So the verse says "it" —
it must be in the north, but the slaughterer need not be in the north.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that backs up the objection in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That the rule 'the שוחט need not be in the צפון' is already known without the נשיא's 'אותו'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אחיא on ויקרא 1:11.

steps.title: 'אותו' excludes a bird from needing צפון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives 'אותו' a new meaning: the goat needs צפון, but a bird offering does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, 'it' must be in the north, but a young bird does not need the north.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing what 'אותו' teaches. Now it is about which kind of offering needs צפון, not about the slaughterer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שוחט rule is already taken, so the word must teach something new. 'אותו' now limits the צפון rule to the animal named, the goat, and leaves out a bird offering. This answer will now need a ברייתא and must hold up against a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: A young bird brought as an offering
Rather (the גמרא switches to a new explanation)

phrases.english: Rather, "it" must be in the north —
but a young bird need not be in the north.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא ״אוֹתוֹ בַּצָּפוֹן״ – וְאֵין בֶּן עוֹף בַּצָּפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 15 by giving 'אותו' a new meaning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the word to a different exclusion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אותו' teaches that the שוחט need not stand in the צפון.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אותו' teaches that a bird offering does not need the צפון.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the קל וחומר that would require צפון for a bird
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that without 'אותו' we would require a bird to be in the צפון, based on a קל וחומר from a sheep.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think a young bird needs the north. And there is a logical argument for it: a young sheep does not need a כהן, yet it needs the north. A young bird does need a כהן, so surely it should need the north too! So the פסוק says 'it'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the new reading. It shows why we would have thought a bird needs צפון, and that 'אותו' blocks this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is a קל וחומר. A sheep is the 'lighter' case, since anyone may slaughter it and no כהן is needed, yet it still needs צפון. A bird is 'stricter', since only a כהן may do מליקה, so it should surely need צפון. 'אותו' is there to stop this conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: It is logical (here it opens a קל וחומר)
A young sheep offering
The תורה fixed a requirement for it
Requires

steps.confusionAlert: 'Did not fix a כהן' does not mean anyone may do the whole עבודה. It refers only to the שחיטה of the sheep, which a non-כהן may do. For a bird, the killing itself (מליקה) needs a כהן.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: יָכוֹל יְהֵא בֶּן עוֹף טָעוּן צָפוֹן?
phrases.english: As it was taught: One might think a young bird requires the north?
And it is logical:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה בֶּן צֹאן, שֶׁלֹּא קָבַע לוֹ כֹּהֵן –
phrases.english: If a young sheep, for which the Torah did not fix a priest,
the Torah still fixed the north for it;
then a young bird, for which it did fix a priest,
is it not logical that it should fix the north for it?
So the verse says: "it."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: יָכוֹל יְהֵא בֶּן עוֹף טָעוּן צָפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 17 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That 'אותו' is needed to exclude a bird from the צפון requirement.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא presenting a קל וחומר from בן צאן to בן עוף.

steps.title: The קל וחומר fails: a sheep needs a utensil
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא breaks the קל וחומר: a sheep needs a כלי for slaughter and a bird does not, so the bird cannot be learned from the sheep.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a young sheep? It is special because the תורה fixed a utensil for it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא's logic. If the קל וחומר does not work, there was never a reason to think a bird needs צפון, so 'אותו' would not be needed for that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sheep must be slaughtered with a knife, but a bird is killed with the כהן's fingernail. Maybe the sheep needs צפון because of that stricter feature. Without the קל וחומר, 'אותו' has no reason to exclude the bird, and the question of what it teaches comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: What about...? (a formula to break a קל וחומר by showing a difference)
A utensil; here, the knife used for שחיטה
Since it is so (points to the special feature)

phrases.english: What about a young sheep?
It is special, since the Torah fixed a utensil for it!
phrases.notes: A sheep needs a knife, but a bird is killed with the כהן's fingernail.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְבֶן צֹאן, שֶׁכֵּן קָבַע לוֹ כְּלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the קל וחומר in the ברייתא of step 18, and with it the answer of step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר from בן צאן to בן עוף, which 'אותו' was said to block.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sheep has a stricter feature, needing a כלי, that a bird lacks. So the קל וחומר fails, and 'אותו' would not be needed to exclude the bird.

steps.title: A new meaning for 'it': the goat needs the north, the קרבן פסח does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the word 'אותו' teaches that the goat must be slaughtered in the צפון, but a קרבן פסח does not need צפון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, 'it' must be in the north, but a פסח does not need to be in the north.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the bird explanation failed, the גמרא gives the word 'אותו' a brand-new job: leaving the קרבן פסח out of the צפון requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 19 the קל וחומר from a sheep to a bird broke, so 'אותו' was not needed to exclude a bird. Now the גמרא says 'אותו' excludes a different offering, the פסח. This keeps the word from being extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (a new answer replaces the old one)
'It': the goat of the נשיא in the פסוק
The קרבן פסח, the Pesach offering

phrases.english: Rather, "it" is in the north
phrases.notes: 'It' is the goat in the פסוק (ויקרא 4:24) that we have been discussing.

phrases.english: but a Pesach offering is not in the north.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed bird explanation from step 17, which step 19 knocked down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra word a new thing to exclude
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אותו' excludes a bird from needing צפון.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אותו' excludes a קרבן פסח from needing צפון.

steps.title: A ברייתא: without 'it' we would have required the north for the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב teaches that a קל וחומר from an עולה would have made a פסח need צפון, so the word 'אותו' is needed to exclude it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says, one might think a פסח needs the north. It seems logical: an עולה has no fixed time for slaughter, yet the Torah fixed the north for it. A פסח does have a fixed time, so surely the Torah would fix the north for it too! That is why the פסוק says 'it'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the new answer. It shows that without 'אותו' we really would have made a פסח need צפון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא argues that the פסח is 'stricter' because it has a fixed time (the afternoon of the 14th of ניסן). So it should at least get the צפון rule that the less strict עולה gets. 'אותו' blocks this reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason (a logical argument is coming)
The Torah fixed a set time for it
Therefore the פסוק says

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
One might think a Pesach offering requires the north?
And it is logical;

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה עוֹלָה, שֶׁכֵּן לָא קָבַע לוֹ זְמַן לִשְׁחִיטָתוֹ –
phrases.english: Just as a burnt offering, for which no time was fixed for its slaughter,
the Torah fixed the north for it;
a Pesach offering, for which a time was fixed for its slaughter,
is it not logical that the north should be fixed for it?
Therefore the verse says: "it."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 20 by showing that a ברייתא uses 'אותו' to exclude the פסח.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that 'אותו' excludes the פסח from צפון
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, built on a קל וחומר from an עולה

steps.title: The burnt offering is special because it is completely burned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא breaks the קל וחומר: an עולה is entirely burned on the מזבח, which a פסח is not, so the פסח cannot be learned from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about an עולה? It is special because it is completely burned!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא's קל וחומר by showing that an עולה has a special strictness the פסח lacks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the 'lighter' case is lighter in every way. An עולה is כליל, completely burned, which makes it holier than a פסח. So its צפון rule may come from that holiness, and it does not carry over to the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: What about an עולה? (it has something special)
Completely burned on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a פסח needs צפון. It is attacking the קל וחומר. If the קל וחומר never worked, then 'אותו' is not needed to exclude the פסח, and the new answer is in trouble.

phrases.english: What about a burnt offering? It is special in that it is entirely burned!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the קל וחומר in the ברייתא of step 21, the same way step 19 challenged the bird קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר from עולה to פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An עולה has its own strictness (כליל) that a פסח lacks, so the עולה is not truly the 'lighter' case.

steps.title: The sin offering is special because it atones for sins punishable by כרת
steps.stepSummary: If we try to learn the פסח from a חטאת instead, that also fails, because a חטאת atones for sins punishable by כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you learn it from a חטאת: what about a חטאת? It is special because it atones for people who are liable to כרת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a different source for the קל וחומר, the חטאת, and knocks that down too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת is not completely burned, so the כליל objection does not apply to it. But a חטאת has its own special strictness: it atones for very serious sins that carry כרת. A פסח does not do that, so it still cannot be learned from a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offering
It atones
People liable to כרת, a punishment of being cut off

phrases.english: From a sin offering? What about a sin offering?
phrases.notes: The גמרא skips the words 'and if you say, learn it' from a חטאת. You have to add them in your head.

phrases.english: It is special in that it atones for those liable to karet!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵחַטָּאת – מָה לְחַטָּאת, שֶׁכֵּן מְכַפֶּרֶת עַל חַיָּיבֵי כָרֵיתוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 22 ruled out the עולה as a source, this step rules out the חטאת as a replacement source.
steps.kashyaTarget: A possible קל וחומר from חטאת to פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חטאת has its own strictness (it atones for sins punishable by כרת) that a פסח lacks, so a פסח cannot be learned from it.

steps.title: The guilt offering cannot teach the פסח either
steps.stepSummary: Learning the פסח from an אשם fails, because an אשם is קדשי קדשים and a פסח is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you try to learn from an אשם: what about an אשם? It is special because it is קדשי קדשים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third offering, the אשם, as the source for a קל וחומר, and knocks it down too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עולה failed because it is fully burned, and the חטאת failed because it atones for sins with כרת. The אשם has neither of those features, but it is still קדשי קדשים. The פסח is a lighter קודש, so the אשם cannot teach it.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt offering
What about...? (the standard way to break a קל וחומר)
Offerings of the most holy level

phrases.english: From a guilt offering —
phrases.notes: He means: and if you try to learn the פסח from an אשם instead.

phrases.english: what about a guilt offering?
It is special in that it is of the most sacred offerings!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of refutations after the עולה and חטאת failed.
steps.kashyaTarget: A קל וחומר from an אשם that would require the פסח to be slaughtered in the צפון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source (אשם) has a stricter status, קדשי קדשים, that the target (פסח) lacks, so the comparison breaks.

steps.title: None of the offerings, even combined, can teach the פסח
steps.stepSummary: Even learning from all three offerings together fails, since all of them are קדשי קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: From all of them together too, it does not work, since they are all קדשי קדשים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the door on learning from any mix of עולה, חטאת, and אשם. They all share a stricter status that the פסח lacks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could try to learn from what the three offerings have in common. But the thing they all have in common is being קדשי קדשים, and that is exactly what makes them stricter than a פסח. So no קל וחומר could ever require צפון for a פסח, and the word 'אותו' is not needed to exclude it.

keyTerms.meaning: From all of them
Also, as well

steps.whatToRemember: No offering, alone or together, can make a פסח need the צפון, because they are all קדשי קדשים. So the word 'אותו' must be teaching something else.

phrases.english: From all of them as well —
phrases.notes: He means learning from the עולה, חטאת, and אשם together.

phrases.english: since they are of the most sacred offerings!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the אשם refutation to every combination, ending this line of reasoning.
steps.kashyaTarget: Any combined derivation of the פסח from all three offerings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The shared feature of all the sources, קדשי קדשים, is absent in the פסח, so even a combined derivation fails.

steps.title: Back to the first reading: the animal in the north, not the slaughterer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to its original explanation of 'אותו': the animal must be in the צפון, but the person slaughtering need not be.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is as we said at first: 'it' must be in the צפון, but the slaughterer does not have to be in the צפון.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the פסח reading fell apart, the גמרא goes back to its first explanation of the word 'אותו'. This sets up the next step, where it will deal with the problem that had been raised against this reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אותו' limits the north requirement to the animal itself. The person doing the שחיטה can stand somewhere else. This reading had been pushed aside earlier, and now the גמרא brings it back.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth (going back to an earlier position)
As we said at the beginning
The one who slaughters
The north side of the עזרה

phrases.english: Actually, it is as we said at first:
"It" is in the north —
phrases.notes: 'It' means the animal itself.

phrases.english: but the one slaughtering is not required to be in the north.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since the פסח reading failed in steps 22 to 25, the גמרא returns to the meaning of 'אותו' first proposed in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Return to an earlier reading of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אותו' had to exclude a פסח from the צפון requirement.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אותו' teaches that the animal is in the צפון but the slaughterer need not be.

steps.title: Not the slaughterer, but the one who collects the blood must be in the north
steps.stepSummary: The objection that רבי אחייא already teaches this is answered: 'אותו' really teaches that the one who collects the blood must stand in the צפון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what bothered you, that we already learn this from רבי אחייא: the word is not there to exclude the slaughterer from the צפון. Rather, it teaches that only the slaughterer need not be in the צפון, but the one who collects the blood must be.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the old problem with the first reading. We already know from רבי אחייא that the slaughterer need not be in the צפון, so 'אותו' must be teaching something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new lesson is an inference. Only the שוחט is free from standing in the צפון, so the מקבל, the כהן collecting the blood, must stand there. That way 'אותו' is not a wasted repeat of רבי אחייא's teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: And what was difficult for you
We derive it
To exclude
The one who collects the blood in a vessel

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two people: the שוחט (slaughterer) may stand anywhere, but the מקבל (the one collecting the blood) must stand in the צפון.

phrases.english: And that which was difficult for you,
that we already derive it from רבי אחייא —
phrases.notes: That's the earlier teaching that already showed the slaughterer doesn't need to stand in the north.

phrases.english: it is not to exclude the slaughterer from being in the north;
rather, only the slaughterer need not be in the north,
but the one who collects the blood must be in the north.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְקַשְׁיָא לָךְ מִדְּרַבִּי אַחִיָּא נָפְקָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the return to the first reading by removing the objection that it repeats רבי אחייא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the פסוק's purpose through an inference
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אותו' is pointless, because רבי אחייא already teaches that the slaughterer need not be in the צפון.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אותו' teaches by inference that the מקבל must stand in the צפון.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule that collecting the blood is done in the צפון, which the rest of the sugya builds on.

steps.title: But the collector rule already comes from 'ולקח'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: we already know the מקבל must be in the צפון from the extra letter in 'ולקח'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule for the one who collects the blood already comes from 'לקח' versus 'ולקח'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new answer. The lesson about the collector is already taught elsewhere, so 'אותו' would again be extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous עמוד, the extra ו in 'ולקח' was read as 'he himself takes'. That taught that the collecting כהן must be in the צפון. If so, 'אותו' cannot be needed for the same lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: "Shall take" / "and shall take": a lesson drawn from the extra letter ו

phrases.english: The one who collects the blood
is derived from "shall take" versus "and shall take"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:34. The extra letter was explained on the previous עמוד as 'he himself takes'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference made in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'אותו' is needed to teach that the מקבל stands in the צפון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy: the same law is already derived from 'ולקח', so 'אותו' would again be unnecessary.

steps.title: This תנא does not learn from 'ולקח'
steps.stepSummary: The תנא behind this teaching does not accept the lesson from the extra ו, so he needs 'אותו' for the collector.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'לקח' versus 'ולקח' does not teach him anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this particular תנא does not learn anything from the extra letter in 'ולקח'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two derivations belong to different opinions. The one who does not learn from 'ולקח' needs another source for the collector standing in the צפון, and 'אותו' gives it to him. So 'אותו' is not wasted.

keyTerms.meaning: It does not imply anything to him (he doesn't learn from it)

phrases.english: "Shall take" versus "and shall take"
does not imply anything to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy objection of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different opinions: this תנא rejects the competing derivation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone learns the collector rule from 'ולקח', so 'אותו' is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: This תנא does not learn from 'ולקח', so he needs 'אותו' to teach the collector rule.
steps.whatToRemember: Final reading of 'אותו': the animal must be in the צפון, the slaughterer need not be, and the collector of the blood must be.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the north is essential?
steps.stepSummary: We have sources that the צפון is the proper way for slaughter and collection of an עולה. Where do we learn that doing them elsewhere disqualifies the offering?
steps.simpleTranslation: We found that slaughter of an עולה in the צפון is a מצוה, and we found that collection there is a מצוה too. But how do we know that slaughter and collection are essential, so the offering is invalid without them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It first sums up what we already know and then asks what is still missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a difference between something that is the right way to do it (למצוה) and something that disqualifies if missing (לעכב). The sources so far only prove the first. The גמרא now looks for a source that the צפון is essential.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source)
As the proper way, but not essential
Essential: without it the offering is invalid
From where do we know?
Collecting the blood in a vessel

steps.confusionAlert: Being 'למצוה' does not mean being 'לעכב'. Something can be the right way to do it and still not invalidate the offering if it is skipped.

phrases.english: We found that slaughter of a burnt offering in the north is a מצוה,
and collecting the blood too, we found, is a מצוה;
from where do we know that slaughter and collection there are essential?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the settled sources for the צפון and asks about a further level, whether the צפון is essential.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that slaughtering and collecting outside the צפון disqualifies an עולה (לעכב), not just that the צפון is the proper way (למצוה).

steps.title: A קל וחומר from the חטאת to the עולה
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה (or רבה בר שילא) argues that since a חטאת, which gets its צפון rule from the עולה, is disqualified outside the צפון, the עולה itself must be disqualified too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said, and some say it was רבה בר שילא: It is a קל וחומר. A חטאת gets its צפון rule from the עולה, and yet doing it outside the צפון disqualifies it. The עולה is the source the חטאת learns from, so isn't it logical that it is also disqualified?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 30 with a logical argument, a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חטאת learns its צפון rule from the עולה, and for a חטאת we know the rule is essential. If the 'student' (חטאת) is disqualified without the צפון, the 'teacher' (עולה) should be disqualified even more.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter case (how much more so)
By the strength of, deriving from
Holds back, meaning it is essential: without it the offering is disqualified
Some say (a different name for who said it)
Is it not logical?

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said,
and some say it was Rabba bar Sheila:
It is learned through an a fortiori argument;
just as a sin offering, whose rule comes by virtue of a burnt offering,
phrases.notes: The חטאת learns its צפון rule from 'במקום העולה' (ויקרא 4:29).

phrases.english: is disqualified without it;
phrases.notes: He means: if a חטאת is not slaughtered or its blood collected in the צפון, it is invalid.

phrases.english: a burnt offering, by whose virtue the sin offering's rule comes,
is it not logical that it is disqualified without it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבָּה בַּר שֵׁילָא: קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 30: where do we learn that the צפון is essential for an עולה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר: if the חטאת, which learns from the עולה, is disqualified outside the צפון, then the עולה surely is.

steps.title: The חטאת is more serious because it atones for כרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the קל וחומר: a חטאת has a special stringency, since it atones for sins punished by כרת, so it may be stricter than an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a חטאת? It is special, because it atones for sins that carry the punishment of כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the קל וחומר by pointing to a way the חטאת is more serious than the עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the source case is not stricter in some way of its own. Since a חטאת atones for very serious sins (כרת) and an עולה does not, maybe only the חטאת is disqualified outside the צפון.

keyTerms.meaning: What about...? (the standard way to point out a difference that breaks a קל וחומר)
Since it has a special quality
Sins that carry the punishment of כרת (being cut off)

phrases.english: What is special about a sin offering?
It is special in that it atones
for sins that make one liable to karet!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְחַטָּאת, שֶׁכֵּן מְכַפֶּרֶת עַל חַיָּיבֵי כָרֵיתוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the קל וחומר of Step 31.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire קל וחומר from חטאת to עולה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The חטאת has its own stringency (atoning for כרת), so its strictness cannot be carried over to the עולה.

steps.title: רבינא: a secondary case is never stricter than its source
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that רב אדא was not bothered by the חטאת's stringency, because he holds that something derived (טפל) can never be stricter than its source (עיקר).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: This is what bothers רב אדא בר אהבה: Have we ever found that a secondary thing is stricter than its main source?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא defends the קל וחומר by explaining how רב אדא would answer the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the חטאת gets its צפון rule from the עולה, the עולה is the main source and the חטאת is secondary. A secondary case cannot be stricter than its source, so if the rule is essential for the חטאת, it must be essential for the עולה. The חטאת's other stringencies don't matter here.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult for him; here: this is the reasoning he holds against the challenge
Have we ever found?
Secondary, the thing that is derived
The main thing, the source

phrases.english: Ravina said:

phrases.aramaic: הָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ לְרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
phrases.english: This is what is difficult for Rav Adda bar Ahava,
phrases.notes: He means: this is the argument רב אדא would raise, which is why the challenge didn't stop him.

phrases.english: have we ever found
a secondary case more stringent than the primary one?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: הָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ לְרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the קל וחומר of Step 31 against the rejection in Step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces a general principle that cancels the challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חטאת's special stringency (atoning for כרת) could make it alone disqualified outside the צפון.
steps.terutzMaskana: A secondary case (חטאת) cannot be stricter than its source (עולה), so the עולה must also be disqualified.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'a טפל is not stricter than its עיקר' is what holds the whole proof together, so the next steps will test whether it is really true.

steps.title: מר זוטרא questions רבינא's rule
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא son of רב מרי challenges רבינא: have we really never found a secondary case stricter than its source?
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא son of רב מרי said to רבינא: And have we not found such a thing?
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא challenges the rule רבינא just stated. This short line sets up the next move, where he will bring an example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even one case shows a secondary thing being stricter than its source, רבינא's defense falls apart, and the challenge from Step 32 against the קל וחומר comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: And not?! (meaning: we certainly have found such a thing)
The son of...

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said to him,
the son of Rav Mari, to Ravina:
And have we not found one?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מָרִי לְרָבִינָא: וְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the principle רבינא used in Step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's rule that a טפל is never stricter than its עיקר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The question is rhetorical: we have found cases where a secondary thing is stricter than its source, so the rule cannot save the קל וחומר.
